Huichuan Scenic Area in Yu County is located in Songzhikouyu, Yu County, Zhangjiakou City, Hebei Province.
It is located at the southwestern foot of Xiaowutai Mountain and is a canyon experience scenic area with primitive natural scenery as the core.
It is the only natural ecological scenic area in the Xiaowutai Mountain area that can be legally developed with the largest single area.

Huichuan Scenic Area is famous for its unique landscape, rich natural ecological resources and diverse tourism experiences, and has become an ideal place for tourists in Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei and surrounding areas to relax, vacation, and escape the summer heat.
The scenic area has rich natural ecological resources, including towering mountains and ridges, canyon waterfalls, primitive forests, strange flowers and plants, and rare animals.
Not only is it a "natural gene bank" and "natural laboratory", it also has the largest primitive forest in North China, providing valuable living space for biodiversity.

The natural landscape in the scenic area includes Nine Waterfalls and Eighteen Pools, Hanging Plank Road, Five Lakes and Four Seas and more than 40 other attractions, each of which has its unique natural beauty and geological features.

Dongling Mountain Night Climb⛰️: Stars and Sea Within Reach🌌 🌙Departure Under the Night Sky🌙 ⛰️Dongling Mountain, the peak of Beijing.
Having experienced several night climbs, I never encountered the ideal starry sky, sunrise, and sea of clouds.
After several days of heavy rain, it was still raining during the day on Friday.

I was hesitant to go, but after checking several weather apps with different forecasts, I decided to take a chance and followed X on the journey to Dongling. 🌟Accompanied by a Sky Full of Stars🌟 🌌 Fortunately, the rain stopped when I left.
There were only two groups due to the rain, and there were many empty seats on the bus, so each person could occupy a row.
When the bus departed, it started raining again.
I rested immediately after taking my seat, and when we arrived at the starting point, the rain had stopped, the sky was clear, and the stars were visible to the naked eye.
It was the first time I saw such a clear starry sky. 🥾Leisurely Night Climb🥾 🌟The most enjoyable part was hiking under the starry sky.
When tired, I looked up at the stars, and there was lightning in the distant valleys.
The night climb was a round-trip route, mainly consisting of steps and boardwalks.
To avoid reaching the cold summit too early, I stayed in a small house at the mid-station of the cable car for a long time to shelter from the wind.
About 1.5 hours before sunrise, I set off.

Near the small house, I tried various angles to photograph the starry sky, using laser pointers, headlamps, and flashlights when taking pictures of people. 🌅Imperfect Sunrise🌅 ⚠️Before reaching the summit, yaks🦬 and cows🐮 may appear.
Be sure to pay attention to the black yaks and walk in groups to avoid disturbing them.
While waiting for the sunrise at the summit, I kept taking silhouette photos and observing the sea of clouds.

Unfortunately, near sunrise, there was always a layer of fog on the horizon, and the sun emerged from the fog, lacking some brilliance. ☁Foggy Sea of Clouds☁ ☄️Although I didn't see the desired sunrise, the sea of clouds was also not ideal, with only a little in the valleys.
It seems that weather forecasts cannot be fully trusted.
However, a few uniquely shaped clouds drifted in from the west, and their colors were brilliant under the morning sun.

I continued taking photos at the summit for a while before reluctantly descending in the morning sun. ⏰Night Climb Reference Time⏰ 🔸00:03 Start hiking 🔸01:30 Arrive at the small house at the cable car station 🔸03:25 Depart from the small house 🔸04:25 Reach the summit 🔸05:23 Sunrise (sunrise time varies, check the forecast in advance) 🔸05:44 Start descending (descend early due to lack of sea of clouds, can descend at 6) 🔸07:40 Reach the endpoint 🔸08:10 Depart for Beijing 📝Notes📝 1️⃣The wind is strong and the temperature is low🥶 at night on Dongling Mountain.
A windbreaker, fleece, thermal blanket, and lightweight down jacket are essential; 2️⃣Load the track in advance, as the signal📶 is poor on the mountain.

Charge headlamps and flashlights in advance, and hang a small bell for night climbing; 3️⃣Respect cows🐮 and yaks🦬, do not approach them when encountered, as they may be grumpy and chew on stones when angry; 4️⃣For photographing the starry sky with a phone📱, set white balance to 4800, exposure to 30s, maximum aperture, and ISO3200.

Zhuolu, Zhangjiakou Starting from Deshengmen in Beijing and heading 130 kilometers north, you can reach Huangdi City in Zhuolu, Hebei.
Huangdi City, also known as Xuanyuan City, is an ancient city site located on the west side of Fanshan Town in Zhuolu County.
It is said that this is the ancient battlefield of the Battle of Banquan between the Yellow Emperor and the Yan Emperor, as well as the Battle of Banquan between the Yellow Emperor and Chiyou.

Here, the Yellow Emperor's tribe united with the Yan Emperor's tribe to defeat Chiyou's tribe, leading to the Yellow Emperor unifying various tribes of China and establishing the first capital city in Chinese history.
To this day, Zhuolu still preserves multiple sites and relics related to the culture of the three ancestors, such as Huangdi Spring, Chiyou's Three Villages, and the Hall of the Three Ancestors.
The Battle of Banquan was a key battle in the establishment of the Huaxia ethnic group.
There are various historical accounts regarding the exact location of the Battle of Banquan.
Some believe it was in the southeast of today's Zhuolu County in Hebei Province, while others think it was within the borders of Changzhi in Shanxi, or Yanqing County in Beijing, or other places.
However, regardless of the exact location, the Battle of Banquan is the most famous battle between the two ancient ancestors of the Chinese nation, the Yellow Emperor and the Yan Emperor.
It holds significant importance in the ultimate formation of the Chinese nation and is therefore regarded as the battle that marked the beginning of Chinese civilization.
Of course, this period of history is still largely in the realm of legend, with not much archaeological evidence to support it.
Even the history of the Xia Dynasty is not yet clear, let alone the history before the Xia Dynasty.
However, people today still tend to believe that this is the ancient battlefield of the Battle of Banquan, providing a focal point for their remembrance.
Today's Zhuolu County is a small, unremarkable, and not very affluent county not far north of Beijing, with no visible traces of the tribal conflicts that took place here five thousand years ago.

📍Zhuolu Museum Recently opened, still not very complete, but the content is rich enough. 🌟Unique architectural style: With the theme of 'Ancient Civilization Begins in Zhuolu', it fully embodies the Chinese cultural concept of 'harmony and unity', promoting the connotation of 'shared bloodline, cultural origin, and national unity'.

The main building is divided into three floors, and its exterior design is inspired by the human-shaped architecture and semi-subterranean covered earth construction methods from the Three Ancestors period. 🌟Rich and exciting exhibits: The museum houses precious cultural relics such as stone flakes, stone cores, and animal bone fossils from the Paleolithic period, showcasing the historical culture of the Zhuolu area and allowing people to deeply understand the development and cultural heritage of this land.
